clinician.trajectory_summary: 47-year-old female with known mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD, diagnosed 2018) and psoriatic arthropathy (diagnosed 2020) presented for annual screening mammography without reported symptoms. Mammography incidentally revealed bilateral axillary lymphadenopathy (16+ nodes on left side, largest 18 mm; 11+ nodes on right side, largest 33 mm) with no suspicious breast findings. This represented a new finding compared to 2017 screening which showed no axillary adenopathy. The mammographic features of the enlarged lymph nodes were not suspicious for malignancy due to their oval shape, visible fatty hilum, and bilateral distribution, suggesting an inflammatory underlying process. The patient was recalled for further assessment and underwent bilateral breast and axillary ultrasound, which confirmed numerous enlarged lymph nodes (largest measuring 30 × 5 mm) with Doppler signal showing intra- and extranodal vascularization, findings that supported an active inflammatory process. The inflammatory nature of the axillary lymphadenopathies was confirmed based on imaging characteristics and clinical context of underlying autoimmune disease.
